stories.head: Bigeye Launches Policy Engine in Agent Trust Hub With Runtime Enforcement Across AI Gateways
stories.plain: Bigeye now lets enterprises define AI policy once and enforce it at runtime across major AI gateways including Kong and Gravitee. As agentic systems act faster than humans can review, this kind of real-time policy enforcement directly shapes how AI agents are bought, governed, and trusted in enterprise settings — a critical procurement and compliance differentiator.

stories.head: Airship Achieves ISO 42001 Certification, Signaling Enterprise AI Governance Benchmark
stories.plain: Airship is among the first customer experience platforms to earn ISO 42001, the global AI management system standard, and positions the cert as a procurement accelerator and EU AI Act readiness signal. Buyers increasingly demand auditable AI governance, so this certification changes how Airship competes in enterprise deals.

stories.head: CreatorIQ Unveils Q, an Enterprise Agentic System for Creator Marketing With Governed AI Agents
stories.plain: CreatorIQ's new product Q brings role-based AI agents to influencer marketing, bundled with measurement (MeasureIQ) and brand-safety tools (SafeIQ). It's a meaningful product launch because it embeds agentic decisioning and governance directly into creator campaign workflows, shifting how brands build and oversee influencer programs at scale.

stories.head: datafuelX Launches AI-Enabled DFX Marketplace for Premium Video With Agentic Buying Workflows
stories.plain: datafuelX opens a marketplace connecting premium video buyers and publishers via agentic workflows and shared intelligence across linear and streaming. This restructures how video ad inventory is transacted — moving from manual negotiation toward automated, AI-driven buying — with direct implications for how marketers allocate video spend.

stories.head: Seismic Launches Role-Based Agentic Revenue Execution With MCP-Powered Workflows
stories.plain: Seismic introduces role-specific AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) workflows that embed trusted company knowledge into sales and marketing actions wherever go-to-market teams work. This matters because MCP-powered agentic integration is becoming a key architecture decision for revenue teams evaluating AI platforms.

stories.head: Bigeye Launches Policy Engine for AI Agents with Runtime Enforcement Across Gateways
stories.plain: Bigeye's new Policy Engine lets enterprises write AI rules once and enforce them live across partners like Kong and Gravitee — stopping agents from taking forbidden actions at runtime, not after the fact. This matters because runtime governance of AI agents is the missing piece most procurement teams are asking for before they greenlight autonomous marketing systems.

stories.head: Airship Earns ISO 42001 Certification, First in CX Industry to Meet Global AI Governance Standard
stories.plain: Airship is among the first customer experience platforms to achieve ISO 42001, the international AI management standard that also helps companies prepare for the EU AI Act. Buyers and procurement teams now have a concrete, third-party benchmark to compare vendors on AI safety — changing how enterprise CX software is evaluated and purchased.

stories.head: CreatorIQ Unveils Q: Governed Agentic System for Enterprise Creator Marketing
stories.plain: CreatorIQ launched Q, a suite of AI agents that handle creator discovery, briefing, and measurement inside a governed framework. Paired with new MeasureIQ and SafeIQ modules, it shows how agentic AI with built-in guardrails is moving into influencer marketing — a channel that has largely been managed manually until now.

stories.head: Seismic Rolls Out Role-Based Agentic Workflows and MCP-Powered Integrations for Go-to-Market Teams
stories.plain: Seismic's new release embeds role-specific AI agents directly into the tools sales and marketing teams already use, connected via Model Context Protocol so agents carry trusted company content into every action. It signals a shift from AI assistants that draft content to agents that actually execute revenue workflows end-to-end.

stories.head: Contentsquare Launches AI-First Experience Platform Spanning Human and Agent Journeys
stories.plain: Contentsquare unified web, mobile, conversation, and LLM signals into one platform that predicts what to fix and pushes changes through design-to-deployment workflows. The key shift: it treats AI agent sessions as first-class journeys alongside human ones — meaning analytics and optimization now must account for non-human traffic, changing how experience data is collected and acted on.

themes.head: The Agentic Layer Becomes Infrastructure
body: Across the month, 'agentic' shifted from buzzword to shipping product. LG Ad Solutions and Magnite are wiring autonomous buying directly into the connected-TV home screen, Seismic is embedding agentic execution into every sales workflow, and CreatorIQ launched an enterprise agentic system for influencer marketing — all in the same news cycle.

The practical decision this forces: stack architecture now has to account for AI agents as first-class actors, not just users. Teams that treat agents as a feature bolt-on will find themselves rebuilding integrations as vendors embed autonomy at the platform level.

Agile Brand · Seismic agentic revenue execution

themes.head: AI Governance Hardens Into Certifications & Runtime Enforcement
body: Governance is moving from policy documents to enforced guardrails. Bigeye shipped a policy engine that applies rules at runtime across AI gateways, while Airship became one of the first MarTech vendors to earn ISO 42001 — the international standard for AI management systems.

The signal for buyers: certifications and runtime controls are becoming a procurement checkbox, not just a trust-marketing claim. Vendors who cannot demonstrate live enforcement will lose deals to those who can, especially in regulated industries.
ev: MarTech Series · Bigeye runtime policy engine

themes.head: The Consumer Trust Gap Widens Against AI Investment
body: Two independent research pieces landed within days of each other showing the same fault line: marketers are accelerating AI and personalization spend while consumers still rank human interaction above algorithmic engagement. The Wunderkind/Cordial study found shoppers prioritise value and convenience; the TFC report confirms people trust people over pixels.

This is a classic over-rotation risk — budgets chasing a capability consumers are actively cool on. The strategically sound move is to use AI to make human touchpoints faster and cheaper, not to replace them, so the brand-side experience still feels personal.
ev: Agile Brand · Wunderkind & Cordial consumer research
Agile Brand · TFC people trust people

themes.head: AI Spend Under the CFO Microscope
body: The Treasure AI CFO interview crystallises a shift happening in boardrooms: AI line items are now large enough to require the same ROI rigour as any capital expenditure. CFOs are asking for usage data, unit economics, and measurable outcomes — not transformation narratives.

For MarTech teams, this changes the buying cycle: tools that cannot surface clear cost-per-outcome metrics will face budget cuts even if they show qualitative value. Vendors are starting to respond — Intuit Intelligence's international rollout, for instance, is framed explicitly around measurable business outcomes for SMBs.
ev: Agile Brand · Treasure AI CFO on AI spend

themes.head: AI Collapses the Video-to-Commerce Workflow
body: Medeo's Creative OS stitches trend discovery, production, and monetisation into a single AI-driven pipeline, while datafuelX launched a marketplace that applies intelligence to premium video trading across linear and streaming simultaneously. Together they signal that AI is collapsing what used to be three separate teams — creative, media, and revenue — into one continuous loop.

For brand and agency planners, this means workflow assumptions built around handoffs are becoming obsolete. The competitive advantage moves to whoever can iterate creative and distribution decisions in near-real-time using unified data, not whoever has the biggest production budget.

Agile Brand · Contentsquare AI-first experience platform

month.takeaway: The month's news resolves into a single underlying pressure: AI is graduating from experimental feature to governed, agent-driven infrastructure — and every budget, workflow, and trust assumption built on the old model now needs to be stress-tested.
